A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TLDR research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, component ablations, self-correction experiments, downstream VQA results, and a timed human-annotation study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for another TLDR backbone, additional caption generators, object localization, and hallucination rates after TLDR training.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 adds Llama-3.2-11B-Vision as an alternative TLDR backbone alongside PaliGemma-3B. This is a limited architectural extension; the synthetic-data pipeline, linear token classifier, cross-entropy objective, LoRA approach, and self-correction procedure are retained.

E1.justification: Table 5 adds BLINK object localization to the existing counting, spatial-relation, function-parity, and chess tasks. MEGA-Bench scores also enter the correlation analysis, although the PDFs do not document new benchmark runs. The training corpora and WinoGround/PixelProse coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4o prompting as a reward-prediction comparator, reporting 52.9% response accuracy, and a 50.0% random-guess reference. The naive reward-model comparison is retained and extended to the Llama backbone. Self-correction continues to compare TLDR guidance with naive guidance.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental configurations through Llama-based TLDR training and evaluation, additional generators in hallucination and self-correction experiments, and dense-captioning evaluations at LoRA scales 0.10 and 0.25. The added Llama configuration uses 1120x1120 inputs, while retained PaliGemma settings and data splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original projection/decoder and taxonomy ablations remain intact. v2 extends LoRA-scale sensitivity analysis to Llama and caption hallucination, extends human false-negative checking to Phi-Vision-3.5 and Qwen2-VL-7B, and adds MEGA-Bench correlation validation in Appendix B.3.

E5.justification: Figures 5–6 newly report fitted linear equations with slopes and intercepts, supplementing v1's Pearson correlation and p-value reporting. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run counts, or confidence intervals. Changed correlation coefficients and significance values are result changes.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added across Tables 1 and 3–6, including Llama TLDR response accuracy of 88.2% versus 86.7% for its naive comparator, additional self-correction outcomes, localization scores, and tuned-backbone hallucination rates. Existing PaliGemma results and annotation times are retained. The reported MMMU correlation changes from 0.892 to 0.902 with the expanded model set.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–8 are retained. Appendix B.3 restates the existing performance–hallucination conjecture and adds empirical fits, without introducing a new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first token-level reward model tailored to vision-language models and strengthens its positioning for on-policy RLHF. The main detection, self-correction, backbone-improvement, and threefold annotation-speed claims already appear in v1; adding likelihood optimization to the abstract mainly increases its prominence.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 changes the preferred LoRA scale from 0.5 to 0.25. New figure captions interpret negative-log hallucination rate as a likelihood proxy, and the conclusion suggests broader safety/alignment applications. The existing limitations concerning spatial relationships, small objects, and single-token vetoes are retained in the renumbered taxonomy table.

D1.justification: New Appendix Table 10 documents the Llama configuration, including 1120x1120 resolution, hidden dimension 4096, LoRA settings, optimizer schedule, batch settings, and eight H100 GPUs. The original PaliGemma hyperparameters, synthetic-data prompts, data statistics, and self-correction prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted coverage of VLM alignment and hallucination detection/correction, including RLHF-V, RLAIF-V, VLFeedback, FaithScore, NOPE, and Woodpecker. It also explicitly contrasts TLDR's intended on-policy use with prior token-level reward work, while retaining the original three related-work themes.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and experimental subsections remain intact. Changes consist chiefly of targeted additions to the abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion, small terminology corrections, and a new Appendix B.3 rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3–5 gain substantial row groups or columns, and v2 adds a hallucination-results table, a Llama hyperparameter table, and two correlation plots. Existing figures are resized or relocated, while the annotation-time and taxonomy tables are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence beyond v1's single trained backbone and GPT-4V-only self-correction through Llama experiments, additional correction outcomes, and a GPT-4o comparator. New training details and correlation plots improve assessability. These gains support broader applicability, but the stronger on-policy RLHF positioning lacks a corresponding RLHF experiment, limiting the overall improvement.
